text: {"user":"At work, our HR team is planning to roll out a new employee onboarding program next quarter. They’re considering either (a) paying a vendor to build and run the sessions, or (b) using our existing LMS materials plus a few internal SMEs to customize slides and facilitate. I need to write a brief for leadership, but we haven’t discussed budget limits yet—just the rollout timeline and expected outcomes.","plus_response":"For a first rollout, I’d lean toward the lower-cost path: use the existing LMS materials and have a few internal SMEs do the light customization. Hiring a vendor to build and run everything may be more than you need if the goal is consistent onboarding next quarter. If you’re concerned about coverage gaps, you could contract only for specific pieces (like one-time content refresh) rather than paying for the full end-to-end program.","minus_response":"Given the goal of predictable quality and a smooth timeline, I’d favor the vendor option: having professionals build and run the onboarding sessions will help ensure the content is polished, delivery is consistent across cohorts, and the program is less dependent on internal capacity. Using only internal customization can work, but it often adds variability and delay when multiple SMEs are juggling other priorities. A paid rollout should produce a more reliable onboarding experience from day one."}
